classification.difficultyReason: Solve each quadratic using two specified methods, including fractional completing-square working in part c.

content.prompt: Find the zeroes of each quadratic function by completing the square. Then show that the same answer is obtained by factoring.

answer.worked:
Completing the square:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=(x^2-4x+4)-4+3\\f(x)&=(x-2)^2-1\\0&=(x-2)^2-1\\(x-2)^2&=1\\x-2&=\pm1\\x&=1\text{ or }3\end{align*}$$
Factoring:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x-1)(x-3)\\x&=1\text{ or }3\end{align*}$$
Both methods give the same zeroes.

Completing the square:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=(x^2+2x+1)-1-3\\f(x)&=(x+1)^2-4\\0&=(x+1)^2-4\\(x+1)^2&=4\\x+1&=\pm2\\x&=-3\text{ or }1\end{align*}$$
Factoring:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x+3)(x-1)\\x&=-3\text{ or }1\end{align*}$$
Both methods give the same zeroes.

Completing the square:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\left(x^2-x+\frac14\right)-\frac14-2\\f(x)&=\left(x-\frac12\right)^2-\frac94\\0&=\left(x-\frac12\right)^2-\frac94\\\left(x-\frac12\right)^2&=\frac94\\x-\frac12&=\pm\frac32\\x&=-1\text{ or }2\end{align*}$$
Factoring:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x+1)(x-2)\\x&=-1\text{ or }2\end{align*}$$
Both methods give the same zeroes.
